meta.title: Terms · YukSaroy
meta.description: YukSaroy terms of use: what the service is, how the subscription is paid and how money is refunded.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.lead: This is not a legal document but a plain agreement: who we are, what we do, how we take money and how we give it back.

s1.h: Who we are and what the service is
s1.p1: YukSaroy is a private site. We are not a state railway organisation and we do not act on behalf of any agency.
s1.p2: The site is a freight logistics marketplace: terminals (rail terminals included), equipment and carriers in one place. Those three categories, nothing else.
s1.p3: A listing is placed by its owner: on equipment and carrier listings the owner writes the price and terms and answers your request. You contact them directly, no middleman.
s1.p4: A terminal page can sit in the catalog before its owner takes it over. Once an ownership claim is confirmed, the owner runs the rates, the slots and the bookings.
s1.p5: The contract and the payment happen between you and the owner, outside the site. We do not carry cargo, do not store it and do not sign documents on behalf of either side.

s2.p1: An account opens with a phone number or with Google. The sign-in code arrives in the Telegram bot.
s2.p2: An account belongs to one person. If you hand your access to someone else, what that account does counts as yours.
s2.p3: The name, organisation and listing text you enter are shown on a public page: you publish them yourself.

s3.p1: The owner answers for the price, the volume and the terms in a listing. We do not check every listing.
s3.p2: The verified badge on a company page means the tax ID (STIR) was checked, it is not a quality guarantee.
s3.p3: Rows with the Demo badge are there to show how the site looks. They have no owner, they are not real offers and messages are never sent to them.
s3.p4: A listing that breaks the rules is taken down. An expired listing leaves the list but stays in your cabinet.

s4.p1: There is one paid thing: the monthly subscription. Catalog, map, comparison, price estimate, listing and chat are free.
s4.p2: What the subscription opens and what it costs is written on the Pricing page. A price change does not affect a period you already paid for.
s4.p3: Payment is manual: you pick the term, the amount and the payment note appear, and we confirm after the transfer. Confirmation usually takes 1 business day, and the subscription starts after it.
s4.p4: There is no booking commission right now. If one is introduced, it will be announced at least 30 days in advance.

s5.p1: Nothing is charged until a payment is confirmed: you cancel a pending order yourself on the subscription page.
s5.p2: Within 7 days of the subscription being switched on, if you have not opened a single phone number and have not used the wagon search, the full amount is returned. On a refund the subscription is switched off and your listings drop back to their usual place in the list.
s5.p3: After that the unused whole months are returned and the month already started is not. For example, if you ask in the second month of a six month subscription, four months come back.
s5.p4: Days when the site itself was down are added to the subscription term: in that case the term is extended rather than money returned.
s5.p5: A subscription closed for breaking the rules is not refunded.
s5.p6: To ask for a refund, write through the Contact page and give the order number. The money goes back to the account it came from within 5 business days.

s6.p1: Not allowed: copying the catalog in bulk, collecting and reselling phone numbers, presenting someone else's object or number as your own, sending adverts in chat.
s6.p2: When a rule is broken the listing is taken down, the account is closed and the subscription is cancelled.
s6.p3: Phone numbers open with a daily limit. That limit is there against catalog copying, and every opening is recorded.
s6.p4: We give a place to meet. We do not answer for the quality of the owner's service, for a delay or for a deal that fell through.
s6.p5: If the terms change, the date at the top is updated. Important changes are announced at least 30 days in advance. If there is a dispute, write to us first: we answer on business days.

s7.p1: The site has five advertising places and we sell them.
s7.p2: We mark every advert with the word Advertisement. Nobody can take that mark off: an advert does not look like a catalog row.
s7.p3: The advert file sits on our own server, so your browser does not go to an outside address. There is no third party code, no pixel and no tracker.
s7.p4: If you click an advert you go to another site.
s7.p5: We refuse a banner that does not fit the rules. The rules are open on the /advertise page.
s7.p6: We count three things: shown, clicked, closed. What stays on the server is a daily total, no IP, no session and no page address.
s7.p7: We do not show adverts to a subscriber.

meta.title: Privacy · YukSaroy
meta.description: What data is collected, why it is kept, who sees it and how it is removed.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: What data is collected, why it is kept, who sees it and how it is removed.

s1.p1: For the account: a phone number, or the email and name from your Google account, and the language you picked. If you set a password, what is kept is not the password itself but its encrypted trace.
s1.p2: What you write yourself: organisation name and tax ID (STIR), listing text and photos, orders, messages, reviews.
s1.p3: For the service to work: sign-in sessions, the IP address a request came from, and a list of important actions on the account, for example that a phone number was opened.
s1.p4: Visit count: the browser sends one empty request once a day. It carries no identifier and no page address; only the IP reaches the server, and the country and region are worked out from it.
s1.p5: What stays in your browser: the language you picked and a sign-in marker live in cookies. The comparison list, the visit date and unfinished form text stay in your browser only and are not sent to the server.

s2.p1: To recognise you and let you into your own account.
s2.p2: To show others the listing and page you published, and to deliver your request to the right owner.
s2.p3: To count the daily limit: without a record of a phone number being opened the limit does not work and the catalog gets copied whole.
s2.p4: To settle disputes: who changed what and when is written down. Data is not sold and not handed to advertising.

s3.p1: Your name, organisation and listing text are public: anyone sees them.
s3.p2: Your phone number is not shown on its own. A subscriber opens it with the Show number button, and every opening is recorded.
s3.p3: Our team sees the data when a request or a dispute needs it.
s3.p4: There are three outside services: the sign-in code arrives through the Telegram bot; if you sign in with Google, Google recognises you; when the map opens the tiles load from the CARTO service.
s3.p5: We name CARTO because it is different: when the map opens your browser connects to that service by itself, and the service sees your IP address. Its terms are on the carto.com/attributions page. The sign-in page does something similar: the code for the Google button loads from a Google server, and Google sees your IP address then, even if you have not clicked anything yet. If you open the site inside the Telegram app, the Telegram code loads the same way. There are no advertising trackers, no pixels and no outside counters.

s4.p2: If you close the account it is made anonymous: the name and contact details are removed. This cannot be undone.
s4.p3: Orders, payments and the action list remain without the account: they are needed for accounting and disputes.
s4.p4: You can clear cookies and browser storage yourself: removing the site data in your browser settings also removes the language choice and the comparison list.

s5.p1: In the cabinet you see and change your own data.
s5.p2: If you want your phone number to stop being opened, pick the Close a number topic on the Contact page.
s5.p3: Use the same form to close the account or to ask what is kept about you.

s6.p1: We use three cookies for signing in. All three are our own, there are no third party cookies.
s6.p2: ys_access: keeps you signed in, lives 15 minutes. Page code cannot read it, only the browser sends it to the server.
s6.p3: ys_refresh: renews the session, so you do not have to sign in again every 15 minutes. Lives 30 days. Page code cannot read this one either.
s6.p4: ys_in: tells the browser that you are signed in, lives 30 days. We made this one readable on purpose: while you are a guest, the page does not send the server a pointless request.
s6.p5: A fourth one is for language: NEXT_LOCALE remembers the language you picked for a year.
s6.p6: Everything else sits in the browser's own storage, on this device only. Nothing of it goes to the server except one item: that is ys-tg-token, and we say more about it below. The lifetime differs too: ys-compare, ys-visit, ys-first-seen, ys-nudge-snooze, ys-ad-quiet, ys-order-draft and the ones starting with ys-admin- stay until you clear them; ys-authed, ys-me, ys-tg-token and the ones starting with ys-req- disappear the moment you close the browser tab.
s6.p7: ys-authed and ys-me: your sign-in marker and a copy of your profile. They are there so the menu does not flicker when a page opens. When you sign out we remove both ourselves.
s6.p8: ys-compare: the comparison basket. ys-visit: so one visit is not counted twice. ys-first-seen and ys-nudge-snooze: the time of your first visit and the snooze time of the sign-up offer.
s6.p9: ys-ad-quiet: the quiet time for adverts. It holds a time number only, which advert it was is not written down. ys-tg-token: the sign-in marker inside the Telegram app. This is the one exception: it goes to the server with every request, because inside the app it takes the place of a cookie. The ones starting with ys-admin-: panel settings, they only exist in a staff browser.
s6.p10: We say this about ys-order-draft and the ones starting with ys-req- separately: they are the drafts of an order and a request you have not sent, so they hold text you wrote yourself, including a contact phone number. We do not take them, they stay in your browser. If you do not need it, you clear it yourself: by sending the form or by removing the site data in your browser settings.
s6.p11: There is no third party cookie and no third party tracker: everything listed above is our own.
s6.p12: The first time you open the site, a consent bar appears at the bottom. It asks permission for exactly four things: ys-first-seen, ys-nudge-snooze, ys-ad-quiet and ys-visit. Your answer is kept in ys-consent, holding the choice and the date, nothing else. That one does not ask for consent itself, because it is what carries your answer out: without it the bar would come back on every page. If you close the bar with the X, nothing is allowed and we ask again on your next visit. ys-consent-later remembers that you closed it until you close the tab.
s6.p13: If you do not allow it, the bottom advert banner is not drawn at all, the sign-up offer is not shown and the visit marker is not sent, so you are not counted in the visit numbers. The necessary cookies and entries listed above are set regardless of consent: signing in, the language choice, the comparison basket and your unsent drafts do not work without them.
